items.title: Show HN: Devbar – Point at what to change. Leave a comment. Your agent ships it
items.why_it_matters: A developer built Devbar, a browser toolbar that lets you point at any UI element on your site, leave a comment, and send the visual context directly to your AI agent to implement. This is perfect for your Next.js projects because instead of taking screenshots and copy-pasting them into Claude to fix CSS or layout bugs, you can annotate your live local site and hand it off. Try installing Devbar on your local project this week, select a UI element you want to tweak, and let Claude Code edit it based on your visual feedback.

items.title: Show HN: Claude's innerworkings: turn 170 costs 2.1x turn 20, over 14,640 turns
items.why_it_matters: An analysis of over 14,000 agent turns revealed that past turn 141, a single turn costs 2.1x more than a turn at the beginning of the same session due to context window accumulation. Since you use Claude Code and Codex daily, letting sessions run too long is quietly draining your token limits and slowing down response times. This week, force yourself to start a fresh session (using `/clear` or opening a new chat) every 25 turns to keep your costs low and Claude's speed high.

items.title: Show HN: A Context Registry for AI coding agents
items.why_it_matters: A new API Context Registry was launched to help coding agents like Claude Code generate production-ready integration code (handling retries, rate-limiting, and auth) without blowing through token limits. When you ask Claude to write backend integrations in Supabase, it often writes basic client calls that fail in production; this registry feeds it the exact context it needs to write robust code. Try pulling a context from this registry the next time you need to connect a third-party service to your Supabase backend this week.

items.title: DiskSpace: Building an app 3 (ok 4) times in a day with Claude
items.why_it_matters: An indie developer shared how they rebuilt a utility app four times in a single day using Claude to test different frameworks and approaches. This is a great reminder that with AI doing the heavy lifting, you don't need to spend weeks planning; you can prototype, throw away, and rebuild an entire app in a few hours. Pick a tiny utility idea you've put off, open Claude Code, and challenge yourself to build a working version of it from scratch before you go to bed tonight.
